        showtickprefix
            If "all", all tick labels are displayed with a prefix.
            If "first", only the first tick is displayed with a
            prefix. If "last", only the last tick is displayed with
            a suffix. If "none", tick prefixes are hidden.
        showticksuffix
            Same as `showtickprefix` but for tick suffixes.
        side
            Determines whether a x (y) axis is positioned at the
            "bottom" ("left") or "top" ("right") of the plotting
            area.
        spikecolor
            Sets the spike color. If undefined, will use the series
            color
        spikedash
            Sets the dash style of lines. Set to a dash type string
            ("solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", or
            "longdashdot") or a dash length list in px (eg
            "5px,10px,2px,2px").
        spikemode
            Determines the drawing mode for the spike line If
            "toaxis", the line is drawn from the data point to the
            axis the  series is plotted on. If "across", the line
            is drawn across the entire plot area, and supercedes
            "toaxis". If "marker", then a marker dot is drawn on
            the axis the series is plotted on
        spikesnap
            Determines whether spikelines are stuck to the cursor
            or to the closest datapoints.
        spikethickness
            Sets the width (in px) of the zero line.
        tick0
            Sets the placement of the first tick on this axis. Use
            with `dtick`. If the axis `type` is "log", then you
            must take the log of your starting tick (e.g. to set
            the starting tick to 100, set the `tick0` to 2) except
            when `dtick`=*L<f>* (see `dtick` for more info). If the
            axis `type` is "date", it should be a date string, like
            date data. If the axis `type` is "category", it should
            be a number, using the scale where each category is
            assigned a serial number from zero in the order it
            appears.
        tickangle
            Sets the angle of the tick labels with respect to the
            horizontal. For example, a `tickangle` of -90 draws the
            tick labels vertically.
        tickcolor
            Sets the tick color.
        tickfont
            Sets the tick font.
        tickformat
            Sets the tick label formatting rule using d3 formatting
            mini-languages which are very similar to those in
            Python. For numbers, see:
            https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format.
            And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-
            format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to
            d3's date formatter: "%h" for half of the year as a
            decimal number as well as "%{n}f" for fractional
            seconds with n digits. For example, *2016-10-13
            09:15:23.456* with tickformat "%H~%M~%S.%2f" would
            display "09~15~23.46"
        tickformatstops
            A tuple of :class:`plotly.graph_objects.layout.yaxis.Ti
            ckformatstop` instances or dicts with compatible
            properties
        tickformatstopdefaults
            When used in a template (as
            layout.template.layout.yaxis.tickformatstopdefaults),
            sets the default property values to use for elements of
            layout.yaxis.tickformatstops
        ticklabelindex
            Only for axes with `type` "date" or "linear". Instead
            of drawing the major tick label, draw the label for the
            minor tick that is n positions away from the major
            tick. E.g. to always draw the label for the minor tick
            before each major tick, choose `ticklabelindex` -1.
            This is useful for date axes with `ticklabelmode`
            "period" if you want to label the period that ends with
            each major tick instead of the period that begins
            there.
        ticklabelindexsrc
            Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for
            `ticklabelindex`.
        ticklabelmode
            Determines where tick labels are drawn with respect to
            their corresponding ticks and grid lines. Only has an
            effect for axes of `type` "date" When set to "period",
            tick labels are drawn in the middle of the period
            between ticks.
        ticklabeloverflow
            Determines how we handle tick labels that would
            overflow either the graph div or the domain of the
            axis. The default value for inside tick labels is *hide
            past domain*. Otherwise on "category" and
            "multicategory" axes the default is "allow". In other
            cases the default is *hide past div*.
        ticklabelposition
            Determines where tick labels are drawn with respect to
            the axis. Please note that top or bottom has no effect
            on x axes or when `ticklabelmode` is set to "period" or
            when `tickson` is set to "boundaries". Similarly, left
            or right has no effect on y axes or when
            `ticklabelmode` is set to "period" or when `tickson` is
            set to "boundaries". Has no effect on "multicategory"
            axes. When used on axes linked by `matches` or
            `scaleanchor`, no extra padding for inside labels would
            be added by autorange, so that the scales could match.
        ticklabelshift
            Shifts the tick labels by the specified number of
            pixels in parallel to the axis. Positive values move
            the labels in the positive direction of the axis.
        ticklabelstandoff
            Sets the standoff distance (in px) between the axis
            tick labels and their default position. A positive
            `ticklabelstandoff` moves the labels farther away from
            the plot area if `ticklabelposition` is "outside", and
            deeper into the plot area if `ticklabelposition` is
            "inside". A negative `ticklabelstandoff` works in the
            opposite direction, moving outside ticks towards the
            plot area and inside ticks towards the outside. If the
            negative value is large enough, inside ticks can even
            end up outside and vice versa.
        ticklabelstep
            Sets the spacing between tick labels as compared to the
            spacing between ticks. A value of 1 (default) means
            each tick gets a label. A value of 2 means shows every
            2nd label. A larger value n means only every nth tick
            is labeled. `tick0` determines which labels are shown.
            Not implemented for axes with `type` "log" or
            "multicategory", or when `tickmode` is "array".
        ticklen
            Sets the tick length (in px).
        tickmode
            Sets the tick mode for this axis. If "auto", the number
            of ticks is set via `nticks`. If "linear", the
            placement of the ticks is determined by a starting
            position `tick0` and a tick step `dtick` ("linear" is
            the default value if `tick0` and `dtick` are provided).
            If "array", the placement of the ticks is set via
            `tickvals` and the tick text is `ticktext`. ("array" is
            the default value if `tickvals` is provided). If
            "sync", the number of ticks will sync with the
            overlayed axis set by `overlaying` property.
        tickprefix
            Sets a tick label prefix.
        ticks

        tickson

        tickvals

You may however group answers / sripts to multiple questions if you find them redundant or can be solved with the same solution s any other of the questions. I want to be sure my concerns are being addressed and that I can understand what will be going on under the hood.
###
b) I fear you might not know enough about the structure and content of the database. Is there any test you would like to run on the database (I use PgAdmin4 as client) before we proceed with the backtest? Lets measure twice or trice before cutting.
###
c) Will we perform a continuous backtest for the entire span of data present in the database or will you divide it in random chunks or blocks of time? (I have no preference)
###
d) How will you determine the 50 or 20 SMA for the first dataset? I ask because there are several days of data that are required to determine the first SMA value of the series. So, for example, if our database covers from March 01, 2020 to June 15, 2025 the first backtest output would start 50 trading days (and not calendar days) after March 01, 2020. This blind period is the needed runway to calculate the 50SMA. Understood?
###
e) How will the script rotate positions? This is how I envision it:
e1: the script starts with a portfolio of N stocks which are bought until the funds are exhausted (US$1MM). Never buy fractional shares. You will round down to the neares integer. But we will never be able to spend the entire budget because there will be a point in which there are no sufficient funds available to purchase any more shares, but the funds willnever reach zero either. We should set a max of N = 15 simultanous positions at any time.
e2: But when / how will the script stop looking for candidates? If N = 15? What if N never reaches 15? What if 4 or 5 stocks exhaust the available funds?
e3: Can we determine to which sector / industry does each stock belong to? We need to avoid over concentration in the same sector. How can we addreess this problem? In real life the trader would do this selection manually, but we have not set a criteris to do this mechanically / rules based. What do you propose?
e4: Once a position is stopped out, does it remain in cash in that position for the rest of the day or does it look for a replacement? And if a replacement is sought, what is the timeframe he has do do so?
e5: To verify if the list of the script's candidates is aligned with the candidates filtered out by TC 2000 we would have to have a list of stocks selected by the script stored in a table for today (T-0) and compare results. They should be very similar in content. Otherwise the script's universe is not aligned with what the user would find in the TC2000 results for today. So the backtest should cover until today (T-0) for selection of candidates, but until the last trading day (T-1) for backtest results. Understood? If so, what is your answer?
###
f) The script must filter out results like $RAMP or $ESPR (screenshots attached), where the stock falls into a rangebound deadzone. These might be takeovers where the company was bought at a certain price and remained flat since then. In reality the user sees this kind of chart from TC2000 and will discard it immediately. So the script has to mimic this ability.
_________________________________
1) See 'b) Database Structure Verification' results attached. I've also performed other tests for your convenience.
2) About 'c) Backtest Span & Chunking': understood and agreed.
3) About 'd) SMA Runway (The Blind Period)': understood and agreed.
4) About 'e) Portfolio Rotation & Capital Mechanics': where's the pivot? We still maintain a strict "0.1% of Global NAV risked per trade." but the capital is not infinite. We start with US$1MM on first day of trading. But I do agree with how you propose we handle the mechanics.
Agreed on e1, e2, e4 and e5, but I must explain our approach on e3: our PostgreSQL database DOES NOT contain a table linking symbols to their sectors. I cannot provide a static CSV mapping tickers to sectors. We will have to live with that.
5) About 'f) Deadzone / Rangebound Filter (The Barcode Charts)': understood and agreed.
###
Where do these input leave us and how will they affect the new script version?

A1: the 10, 20, and 50 SMAs MUST be calculated using the Daily closes.
A2: Yes, I agree with the "Ratchet Rule": Once the R-Multiple is hit, the active stop becomes MAX(Initial_Stop, Trailing_SMA).
A3: regarding 'Overnight Gap-Down Execution', I agree with your 'gap-down slippage' solution.
